_instructions: Score every hint for the pair it sits under. 'already_served' is context only: do not score it.

hints.explanation: Ancient history is the far past, and Ancient Aliens is the famously meme-able series on the History channel.

lines.ALIEN: Ancient Aliens asks whether aliens visited early humans.
lines.HISTORY: Ancient history covers the earliest civilizations.

hints.explanation: The famous statue Venus de Milo is missing both arms, and Venus is the second planet from the Sun.

lines.ARM: The ancient Venus de Milo statue has no arms.
lines.PLANET: Venus is the hottest planet in the solar system.

hints.explanation: A golf caddy carries the player's bag, and a tea caddy is a tin for storing tea.

lines.BAG: Golf caddies carry the bag around the course.
lines.TEA: A tea caddy is a container for loose tea.

hints.explanation: An oasis is a green spot of water in the desert, and Oasis is the British band behind "Wonderwall."

lines.BAND: Oasis sang "Wonderwall" and "Don't Look Back in Anger."
lines.DESERT: An oasis is a desert watering hole.

hints.explanation: Dogs bark and bite, and someone's "bark is worse than their bite."

lines.BITE: Dogs can bite, and the saying says their bark is worse.

hints.explanation: In basketball a jumper is a jump shot, and jumper cables bring a dead car battery back to life.

lines.BATTERY: Jumper cables connect a dead battery to a working one.
lines.SHOT: A jumper is basketball slang for a jump shot.

hints.explanation: At a restaurant you ask for the check, meaning the bill, and in chess "check" means the king is under attack.

lines.BILL: The check is the bill at a restaurant.
lines.CHESS: Check, and then checkmate, in chess.

hints.explanation: During a total lunar eclipse, the moon turns red and is called a blood moon.

lines.BLOOD: A blood moon happens during an eclipse.
lines.MOON: A lunar eclipse darkens the moon.

hints.explanation: Harry Potter has a lightning-bolt scar, and Scar is the villainous lion in The Lion King.

lines.BOLT: Harry Potter's forehead scar is shaped like a lightning bolt.
lines.LION: Scar is Simba's wicked uncle in The Lion King.

hints.explanation: You pop a bubble, and Pop is a nickname for Dad.

lines.FATHER: Pop is a familiar name for a father.

hints.explanation: Mars is the Red Planet, and Mars is the company behind candy like M&M's and Snickers.

lines.CANDY: Mars is a big candy maker.
lines.RED: Mars is known as the Red Planet.

hints.explanation: Tom Thumb is the tiny hero of the old fairy tale, and Tom is the cat in Tom and Jerry (a male cat is also called a tomcat).

lines.CAT: Tom is the cat forever chasing Jerry, and a tomcat is a male cat.
lines.THUMB: Tom Thumb is a fairy tale boy no bigger than his father's thumb.

hints.explanation: Hurdles are a track event, and a hurdle is any challenge to get over.

lines.CHALLENGE: A hurdle is a challenge to overcome.
lines.TRACK: Runners jump hurdles on the track.

hints.explanation: Mars was the Roman god of war, and Mars is also the candy company behind the Mars bar.

lines.CHOCOLATE: The Mars bar is a chocolate candy bar.
lines.WAR: Mars is the Roman god of war, and the red planet is named after him.

hints.explanation: P. T. Barnum billed his circus as the Greatest Show on Earth.

lines.CIRCUS: Barnum built a famous traveling circus.
lines.SHOW: The Greatest Show on Earth was Barnum's slogan.

hints.explanation: In card games the joker is often wild, and Batman's villain the Joker is a clown.

lines.CLOWN: The Joker is Batman's clown-faced enemy.
lines.WILD: "Jokers wild" means the joker can stand for any card.

hints.explanation: In The Polar Express, a train conductor punches the children's tickets on the way to the North Pole.

lines.CONDUCTOR: The Polar Express has a famous train conductor.
lines.POLAR: The Polar Express is the Christmas train story.

hints.explanation: You reboot a computer after it crashes, and Hollywood loves to reboot old film series.

lines.CRASH: Rebooting is the classic fix after a crash.
lines.FILM: A reboot restarts a film franchise from scratch.

hints.explanation: An X is a cross shape, and on pirate maps X marks the spot where the treasure is buried.

lines.CROSS: An X is a cross, as in kisses or a crossed-out answer.
lines.TREASURE: "X marks the spot" is the classic treasure map clue.

hints.explanation: Dessert is usually the last course of a meal, and golf is played on a course.

lines.DESSERT: Dessert is usually the final course.
lines.GOLF: Golf is played on a golf course.

hints.explanation: Abbott and Costello's comedy routine is "Who's on First?", and Doctor Who is the time-traveling TV hero.

lines.DOCTOR: Doctor Who travels through time in the TARDIS.
lines.FIRST: "Who's on First?" is a classic baseball comedy sketch.

hints.explanation: A drill sergeant trains new soldiers.

lines.DRILL: A drill sergeant runs boot-camp drills.
lines.SOLDIER: A sergeant is a soldier's rank.

hints.explanation: The White House holds an Easter Egg Roll, and an egg roll is a crispy snack.

lines.EASTER: Easter eggs are hunted every spring.
lines.ROLL: An egg roll is a fried snack.

hints.explanation: Tinker Bell is Peter Pan's fairy, named because she mends pots and kettles like a tinker.

lines.FAIRY: Tinker Bell is the most famous fairy in Neverland.
lines.PAN: Tinker Bell is Peter Pan's loyal companion.

hints.explanation: Pixar's Coco is set in Mexico on the Day of the Dead, and Coco Chanel is a legend of fashion.

lines.FASHION: Coco Chanel created the little black dress and Chanel No. 5.
lines.MEXICO: Coco follows Miguel through a Mexican Day of the Dead.

hints.explanation: May the Fourth is Star Wars Day, and the Fourth of July means fireworks.

lines.FIREWORKS: The Fourth of July is celebrated with fireworks.
lines.STAR WARS: May the Fourth be with you is the Star Wars Day pun.

hints.explanation: The tomato is botanically a fruit but is usually cooked and served as a vegetable.

lines.FRUIT: Botanically, a tomato is a fruit.
lines.VEGETABLE: Tomatoes are treated as vegetables in the kitchen.

hints.explanation: In the Bible, Samson was super strong until his hair was cut.

lines.HAIR: Samson's strength was tied to his uncut hair.

hints.explanation: Hook, line, and sinker are the parts of a fishing rig, and the phrase means believing something completely.

lines.HOOK: Hook, line, and sinker go together.
lines.LINE: A sinker weighs down the fishing line.

hints.explanation: Jam and pickles both come in jars, and being in a jam or in a pickle both mean being in trouble.

lines.PICKLE: Pickles are sold in jars too.

hints.explanation: A kiwi fruit has fuzzy brown skin, and the fuzz is old slang for the police.

lines.KIWI: Kiwi fruit is covered in fuzz.
lines.POLICE: The fuzz is slang for the police.

hints.explanation: In Mario games, Koopa Troopas are turtles whose shells you can kick and throw.

lines.MARIO: Koopa Troopas are classic Mario enemies.
lines.SHELL: A Koopa's shell becomes a weapon when kicked.

hints.explanation: Thin Mints are the best-known Girl Scout cookie, chocolate-coated with a mint flavor.

lines.MINT: Mint gives Girl Scout Thin Mints their cool flavor.
lines.THIN: Thin Mints are a famous Girl Scout cookie.

hints.explanation: Shredder is the ninja villain of the Ninja Turtles, and a paper shredder cuts documents to strips.

lines.NINJA: Shredder leads the Foot Clan of ninjas.

hints.explanation: On the bridge of Khazad-dum, Gandalf slams down his staff and shouts "You shall not pass!"

lines.PASS: "You shall not pass!" is Gandalf's famous line.
lines.STAFF: Gandalf the wizard carries a wooden staff.

hints.explanation: Bugs munch on plants, and spies plant bugs to listen in on secret talks.

lines.SPY: A spy's bug is a hidden microphone.

hints.explanation: In the Looney Tunes cartoons, Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck shout "Rabbit season!" "Duck season!" at the hunter Elmer Fudd, who is always chasing that rabbit.

lines.RABBIT: Elmer Fudd is forever hunting Bugs Bunny, the wascally wabbit.
lines.SEASON: Bugs and Daffy argue over whether it is rabbit season or duck season.

hints.explanation: The Roomba is a robot vacuum that cleans floors on its own.

lines.ROBOT: A Roomba is a little floor-cleaning robot.
lines.VACUUM: A Roomba is a vacuum cleaner.

hints.explanation: Dorothy is swept to Oz by a tornado and meets the Scarecrow on the yellow brick road.

lines.SCARECROW: The Scarecrow joins Dorothy to ask the Wizard for a brain.
lines.TORNADO: A Kansas tornado carries Dorothy's house to Oz.

hints.explanation: In Greek myth Medusa has snakes for hair and turns anyone who looks at her to stone.

lines.SNAKE: Medusa's hair is a nest of living snakes.
lines.STONE: Medusa's gaze turns people to stone.

hints.explanation: Plankton is SpongeBob's tiny villain who schemes for the Krabby Patty formula, and many whales feed on plankton.

lines.SPONGEBOB: Plankton plots against SpongeBob and Mr. Krabs.
lines.WHALE: Blue whales eat tiny plankton and krill.

hints.explanation: In Greek myth, Icarus flew too close to the sun and the wax on his wings melted.

lines.WING: Icarus flew on wings of feathers and wax.

hints.explanation: You answer to the boss at work, and a video game level often ends with a boss fight.

lines.VIDEO GAME: A boss is the big enemy at the end of a game level.
lines.WORK: The boss runs things at work.
